claim: Clustered ion channels at nodes of Ranvier are critical for fast action potential propagation in myelinated axons.
source: Clustered ion channels at nodes of Ranvier are critical for fast action potential propagation in myelinated axons.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data from this manuscript.

claim: Axon-glia interactions converge on ankyrin and spectrin cytoskeletal proteins to cluster nodal Na+ channels during development.
source: Axon-glia interactions converge on ankyrin and spectrin cytoskeletal proteins to cluster nodal Na+ channels during development.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data from this manuscript.

claim: β4 spectrin is the primary spectrin at nodes of Ranvier.
source: We demonstrate a hierarchy of nodal spectrins, where β4 spectrin is the primary spectrin and β1 spectrin can substitute; each is sufficient for proper node organization.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing β4 spectrin is normally present at nodes and β1 spectrin appears when β4 is absent.

claim: β1 spectrin can substitute for β4 spectrin at nodes of Ranvier.
source: We demonstrate a hierarchy of nodal spectrins, where β4 spectrin is the primary spectrin and β1 spectrin can substitute; each is sufficient for proper node organization.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data showing β1 spectrin at nodes in β4 spectrin knockout mice.

claim: Mice lacking nodal β spectrins have normal nodal Na+ channel clustering during development.
source: Remarkably, mice lacking nodal β spectrins have normal nodal Na+ channel clustering during development, but progressively lose Na+ channels with increasing age.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data at postnatal day 8 showing Nav channels at nodes in double knockout mice.

claim: Mice lacking nodal β spectrins progressively lose Na+ channels with increasing age.
source: Remarkably, mice lacking nodal β spectrins have normal nodal Na+ channel clustering during development, but progressively lose Na+ channels with increasing age.
evidence: This is supported by quantification showing progressive decrease in percentage of nodes with Nav channels from P8 to 6 months.

claim: Loss of nodal spectrins is accompanied by an axon injury response.
source: Loss of nodal spectrins is accompanied by an axon injury response and axon deformation.
evidence: This is supported by ATF3 immunostaining data showing increased injury marker expression in DRG neurons.

claim: Loss of nodal spectrins is accompanied by axon deformation.
source: Loss of nodal spectrins is accompanied by an axon injury response and axon deformation.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing decreased axon circularity in knockout mice.

claim: Nodal spectrins are required to maintain nodal Na+ channel clusters.
source: Thus, nodal spectrins are required to maintain nodal Na+ channel clusters and the structural integrity of axons.
evidence: This is supported by data showing progressive loss of Nav channels at nodes in aged double knockout mice.

claim: Nodal spectrins are required to maintain the structural integrity of axons.
source: Thus, nodal spectrins are required to maintain nodal Na+ channel clusters and the structural integrity of axons.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data showing axon deformation and altered circularity.

claim: Disruption of nodes occurs in many neurological diseases and injuries.
source: Disruption of nodes occurs in many neurological diseases and injuries (Craner et al., 2004; Nashmi and Fehlings, 2001; Susuki, 2013), and discovery of the basic mechanisms that cluster and maintain nodal ion channels may lead to therapeutic approaches to repair, preserve, and rebuild nodes.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Two distinct neuron-glia interactions converge on the axonal cytoskeleton to cluster nodal ion channels during development.
source: Previous studies revealed that two distinct neuron-glia interactions converge on the axonal cytoskeleton to cluster nodal ion channels during development (Amor et al., 2017; Feinberg et al., 2010; Susuki et al., 2013; Zonta et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of nodal extracellular matrix molecules results in the gradual reduction of nodal voltage-gated Na+ channel density.
source: Previous studies showed that loss of nodal extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules results in the gradual reduction of nodal voltage-gated Na+ (Nav) channel density (Amor et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: β4 spectrin has been proposed to stabilize nodes.
source: In addition, the AnkG-binding and node-enriched cytoskeletal protein β4 spectrin has been proposed to stabilize nodes (Berghs et al., 2000; Komada and Soriano, 2002; Lacas-Gervais et al., 2004; Yang et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Human patients with pathogenic variants of SPTBN4 have severe intellectual disability, hypotonia and motor axonal neuropathy.
source: We recently reported human patients with pathogenic variants of SPTBN4, the gene encoding β4 spectrin (Wang et al., 2018). These patients have severe intellectual disability, hypotonia and motor axonal neuropathy.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: Mice lacking β4 spectrin have ataxia, reduced lifespan, and reduced nodal Nav channel density.
source: Similarly, mice lacking β4 spectrin have ataxia, reduced lifespan, and reduced nodal Nav channel density (Berghs et al., 2000; Komada and Soriano, 2002; Lacas-Gervais et al., 2004; Yang et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Patients and mice with pathogenic β4 spectrin variants have normal peripheral sensory axon function.
source: However, these patients and mice have normal peripheral sensory axon function (Wang et al., 2018; Yang et al., 2004), and the percentage of nodes with Nav channels is unchanged (Ho et al., 2014; Susuki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: βI spectrin is located at nodes in β4 spectrin mutant mice.
source: We found that βI spectrin, the major β spectrin in erythrocytes, is located at nodes in β4 spectrin mutant mice (Ho et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: β1 spectrin may partially compensate for loss of β4 spectrin to maintain nodal Nav channels and sensory axon function.
source: Thus, β1 spectrin may partially compensate for loss of β4 spectrin to maintain nodal Nav channels and sensory axon function.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that β1 spectrin is present at nodes in β4 spectrin mutant mice and sensory function is preserved.

claim: Axon initial segments are highly enriched with β4 spectrin.
source: AIS are highly enriched with β4 spectrin and function to both initiate action potentials and regulate the proper trafficking and sorting of somatodendritic and axonal cargoes (Leterrier, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Axon initial segments function to initiate action potentials and regulate the proper trafficking and sorting of somatodendritic and axonal cargoes.
source: AIS are highly enriched with β4 spectrin and function to both initiate action potentials and regulate the proper trafficking and sorting of somatodendritic and axonal cargoes (Leterrier, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Many pseudounipolar sensory neurons in the dorsal root ganglia are myelinated with nodes of Ranvier but lack an AIS.
source: Pseudounipolar sensory neurons in the dorsal root ganglia in vivo may be an excellent experimental system to test the function of nodal β spectrins since many are myelinated with nodes of Ranvier, but most lack an AIS (Gumy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Mice lacking α2 spectrin in sensory neurons had profound defects in node of Ranvier assembly and showed axon degeneration.
source: We previously generated mice lacking α2 spectrin, the only neuronal α spectrin and obligate binding partner for β1 and β4 spectrin, in sensory neurons. These mice had profound defects in node of Ranvier assembly and showed axon degeneration (Huang et al., 2017b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: α2 spectrin is found throughout the neuron and not only at nodes.
source: However, these pathologies cannot be ascribed solely to loss of nodal spectrins since α2 spectrin is found throughout the neuron and not only at nodes (Huang et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: Cre-dependent recombination in Sptbn4F/F mice effectively eliminates both β4Σ1 and β4Σ6 spectrin splice variants.
source: These results show that Cre-dependent recombination in Sptbn4F/F mice effectively eliminates both β4Σ1 and β4Σ6 spectrin splice variants.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting and immunostaining data shown in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: There is no significant difference in latency to fall on an accelerating rotarod between 1.5 month-old Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: We found no significant difference between 1.5 month-old Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F groups (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 1C with p=0.9708.

claim: There is no significant difference in hot plate test latency between 1.5 month-old Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: We found no significant difference between 1.5 month-old Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F groups (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 1D with p=0.5003.

claim: There is no difference in compound action potential shape or conduction velocity in dorsal roots between Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: We found no difference in CAP shape or conduction velocity (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 1E and 1F with p=0.9202.

claim: β4 spectrin is not required for sensory axon function.
source: These results show that sensory neuron function and action potential propagation are intact in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice, and that β4 spectrin is not required for sensory axon function.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral and electrophysiological data showing no deficits in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.

claim: β4 spectrin is lost from dorsal root nodes in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Although we confirmed loss of β4 spectrin from dorsal root nodes in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice, Nav channels were still enriched at nodes (Figure 1G,H)
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1G and quantification in Figure 1H.

claim: Nav channels are still enriched at nodes in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice despite loss of β4 spectrin.
source: Although we confirmed loss of β4 spectrin from dorsal root nodes in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice, Nav channels were still enriched at nodes (Figure 1G,H)
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1G and quantification in Figure 1H.

claim: There is no difference in the percentage of nodes with Nav channels at 6 months of age between Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: even at 6 months of age we observed no difference in the percentage of nodes with Nav channels (not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from data not shown in the manuscript.

claim: Mean node lengths are 1.38 ± 0.05 μm in Sptbn4F/F mice and 1.55 ± 0.12 μm in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice with no significant difference (p=0.28).
source: We also measured node length and found mean node lengths of 1.38 ± 0.05 μm and 1.55 ± 0.12 μm (± SEM, p=0.28) in Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by direct measurement data.

claim: β4 spectrin is dispensable for nodal Nav channel clustering.
source: These results show that β4 spectrin is dispensable for nodal Nav channel clustering.
evidence: This is inferred from data showing Nav channels remain at nodes despite loss of β4 spectrin.

claim: β1 spectrin was found at all nodes in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Immunostaining showed that β1 spectrin was found at all nodes in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice (Figure 2A,C).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2A and quantification in Figure 2C.

claim: Nodal AnkR was significantly increased in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Similarly, we found that nodal AnkR was significantly increased while nodal AnkG decreased in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2B and quantification in Figure 2C showing p=0.0002.

claim: Nodal AnkG decreased in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Similarly, we found that nodal AnkR was significantly increased while nodal AnkG decreased in Avil-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2B and quantification in Figure 2C showing p=0.0014.

claim: A hierarchy of spectrins and ankyrins exists at nodes of Ranvier where a primary complex consists of β4 spectrin and AnkG, but when either is absent, a secondary complex consisting of β1 spectrin and AnkR can substitute.
source: These results support the existence of a hierarchy of spectrins and ankyrins at nodes of Ranvier (Ho et al., 2014). The primary complex consists of β4 spectrin and AnkG, but when either β4 spectrin or AnkG are absent, a secondary complex consisting of β1 spectrin and AnkR can substitute.
evidence: This is supported by the immunostaining data showing β1 spectrin and AnkR at nodes when β4 spectrin is absent, and by citation to previous work.

claim: Nes-Cre;SptbF/F mice show complete removal of neuronal β1 spectrin.
source: Immunoblotting of brain homogenate and immunostaining of brain sections showed complete removal of neuronal β1 spectrin in Nes-Cre;SptbF/F mice (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting and immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: There is no significant difference in rotarod performance between SptbF/F and Avil-Cre;SptbF/F mice.
source: Behavioral and electrophysiological results showed no significant differences between control and Avil-Cre;SptbF/F mice (Figure 3C–F).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 3C with p=0.2706.

claim: There is no significant difference in hot plate test between SptbF/F and Avil-Cre;SptbF/F mice.
source: Behavioral and electrophysiological results showed no significant differences between control and Avil-Cre;SptbF/F mice (Figure 3C–F).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 3D with p=0.4403.

claim: There is no significant difference in conduction velocity between SptbF/F and Avil-Cre;SptbF/F mice.
source: Behavioral and electrophysiological results showed no significant differences between control and Avil-Cre;SptbF/F mice (Figure 3C–F).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 3E and 3F with p=0.7562.

claim: β4 spectrin and Nav channels are normally clustered at nodes in 1.5 month-old Avil-Cre;SptbF/F mice.
source: Furthermore, immunostaining of sensory roots from 1.5 month-old Avil-Cre;SptbF/F mice showed that β4 spectrin and Nav channels are normally clustered at nodes (Figure 3G–H).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3G and quantification in Figure 3H.

claim: β1 spectrin does not normally contribute to Nav channel clustering or peripheral sensory neuron function.
source: Together, these results support the notion of a hierarchy of nodal spectrin function and show that β1 spectrin does not normally contribute to Nav channel clustering or peripheral sensory neuron function.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of phenotype in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F mice.

claim: Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice have severe defects in proprioception as indicated by hindlimb clasping.
source: We found that Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice had severe defects in proprioception as indicated by hindlimb clasping (Figure 4A) and gait analysis (Figure 4B and Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by observation shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice have severe defects in proprioception as indicated by gait analysis.
source: We found that Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice had severe defects in proprioception as indicated by hindlimb clasping (Figure 4A) and gait analysis (Figure 4B and Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by gait analysis shown in Figure 4B and Video 1.

claim: Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice have impaired performance on the accelerating rotarod.
source: These impairments prevented Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice from remaining on the accelerating rotarod (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by rotarod test data shown in Figure 4C with p=7.17995E-09.

claim: Nociception as assayed by the tail immersion test shows no significant difference between SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: However, consistent with a specific impairment at nodes of Ranvier, nociception as assayed by the tail immersion test, showed no significant difference in the latency to tail flick (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by tail immersion test data shown in Figure 4D with p=0.2011.

claim: Both amplitude and velocity of compound action potentials were significantly decreased in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Furthermore, we measured compound action potentials in dorsal roots and found both amplitude and velocity were significantly decreased in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice (Figure 4E,F).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data shown in Figure 4E and 4F with p=2.76334E-14.

claim: Mice lacking both β4 and β1 spectrins have severely compromised myelinated sensory axon function.
source: Thus, mice lacking both β4 and β1 spectrins have severely compromised myelinated sensory axon function.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral and electrophysiological deficits observed in double knockout mice.

claim: In the absence of β4 and β1 spectrins, Nav channels were appropriately clustered at nodes at postnatal day 8.
source: Surprisingly, in the absence of β4 and β1 spectrins we found Nav channels were appropriately clustered at nodes at postnatal day 8 (Figure 5A,B)
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5A and quantification in Figure 5B showing no significant difference at P8 (p=0.3508).

claim: There is no difference in the total number of nodes between SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice at 1 or 6 months of age.
source: we found no difference in the total number of nodes between SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F and Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice at 1 or 6 months of age (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by quantification shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The number of nodes with nodal Nav channels in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice progressively decreased with increasing age such that by 6 months of age only ~40% of nodes had Nav channels.
source: However, compared to SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice, the number of nodes with nodal Nav channels in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice progressively decreased with increasing age such that by 6 months of age only ~40% of nodes had Nav channels (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5A and quantification in Figure 5B.

claim: Nodes in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice have both AnkR and AnkG.
source: Immunostaining also revealed that nodes in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice had both AnkR and AnkG (Figure 5C), since both can bind to NF186 (Ho et al., 2014), but the number of nodes with ankyrins decreased with increasing age.
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data and citation to previous work.

claim: The number of nodes with ankyrins decreased with increasing age in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Immunostaining also revealed that nodes in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice had both AnkR and AnkG (Figure 5C), since both can bind to NF186 (Ho et al., 2014), but the number of nodes with ankyrins decreased with increasing age.
evidence: This is supported by quantification shown in Figure 5C showing significant decrease from 1 month to 6 months (p=0.0296).

claim: The absence of β4 and β1 spectrin did not affect paranodal axon-glia interactions in 6 month-old Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Despite the significant loss of nodal Nav channels in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice, the absence of β4 and β1 spectrin did not affect paranodal axon-glia interactions (as indicated by Caspr immunostaining) or juxtaparanodal domains (as indicated by Kv1.2 immunostaining) in 6 month-old Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The absence of β4 and β1 spectrin did not affect juxtaparanodal domains in 6 month-old Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Despite the significant loss of nodal Nav channels in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice, the absence of β4 and β1 spectrin did not affect paranodal axon-glia interactions (as indicated by Caspr immunostaining) or juxtaparanodal domains (as indicated by Kv1.2 immunostaining) in 6 month-old Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The nodal spectrin cytoskeleton does not contribute to the initial clustering of Nav channels.
source: Together, these results show that the nodal spectrin cytoskeleton does not contribute to the initial clustering of Nav channels, but instead is required to maintain Nav channels and ankyrins at nodes.
evidence: This is inferred from data showing Nav channels cluster normally at P8 in double knockout mice.

claim: The nodal spectrin cytoskeleton is required to maintain Nav channels and ankyrins at nodes.
source: Together, these results show that the nodal spectrin cytoskeleton does not contribute to the initial clustering of Nav channels, but instead is required to maintain Nav channels and ankyrins at nodes.
evidence: This is supported by data showing progressive loss of Nav channels and ankyrins with age in double knockout mice.

claim: β2 spectrin was not detected at nodes in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: We did not detect either of these β spectrins at nodes (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: β3 spectrin was not detected at nodes in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: We did not detect either of these β spectrins at nodes (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Despite expression of β2 and β3 spectrin in axons, only β1 spectrin or β4 spectrin can function at nodes to maintain Nav channels.
source: Thus, despite expression of β2 and β3 spectrin in axons, only β1 spectrin or β4 spectrin can function at nodes to maintain Nav channels.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of β2 and β3 spectrin at nodes and the phenotype of double knockout mice.

claim: Loss of α2 spectrin causes axon degeneration.
source: Loss of α2 spectrin causes axon degeneration (Huang et al., 2017a; Huang et al., 2017b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of internodal β2 spectrin does not cause axon degeneration in PNS sensory axons.
source: However, loss of internodal β2 spectrin does not cause axon degeneration in PNS sensory axons (Zhang et al., 2013), suggesting that loss of the nodal cytoskeleton alone may be sufficient to drive axon injury and degeneration in sensory neurons lacking an AIS.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: There is no significant difference in ATF3 expression among all genotypes in 1 month-old mice.
source: We found no significant difference among all genotypes in 1 month-old mice (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by quantification shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The percentage of ATF3 positive DRG neurons was dramatically and significantly increased in neurons lacking both β1 and β4 spectrin in 6 and 9+ months-old mice.
source: However, the percentage of ATF3 positive DRG neurons was dramatically and significantly increased in neurons lacking both β1 and β4 spectrin in 6 and 9+ months-old mice (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and quantification in Figure 6B.

claim: No ATF3 labeling was detected in DRG neurons in mice lacking only a single β spectrin.
source: However, we did not detect any ATF3 labeling of DRG neurons in mice lacking only a single β spectrin.
evidence: This is supported by quantification shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Large diameter neurons were more likely to be ATF3+ in Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Consistent with the behavioral phenotypes, we found that large diameter neurons were more likely to be ATF3+ (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F axons were deformed and irregular compared to control mice.
source: Compared to control mice, Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F axons were deformed and irregular (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy images shown in Figure 6D and quantification of circularity in Figure 6E.

claim: Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F axons are more myelinated than axons from SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Measurement of the g-ratio suggested that Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F axons are more myelinated than axons from SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice (Figure 6F,G).
evidence: This is supported by g-ratio measurements shown in Figure 6F and 6G with p=0.0045.

claim: The mean diameter of axons lacking nodal β spectrins is significantly less than that for control axons.
source: Furthermore, quantification of axon diameter revealed the mean diameter of axons lacking nodal β spectrins is significantly less than that for control axons (Figure 6H,I).
evidence: This is supported by quantification shown in Figure 6H and 6I with p=0.0023.

claim: Loss of nodal β spectrins alone is sufficient to disrupt axon structure and induce an axon injury response.
source: In summary, loss of nodal β spectrins alone is sufficient to disrupt axon structure and induce an axon injury response.
evidence: This is inferred from the ATF3 expression and electron microscopy data in double knockout mice.

claim: Clustering of Nav channels at nodes of Ranvier is essential for efficient action potential propagation.
source: Clustering of Nav channels at nodes of Ranvier is essential for efficient action potential propagation and has been proposed as a key event in the evolution of complex nervous systems (Hill et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Clustering of Nav channels at nodes of Ranvier has been proposed as a key event in the evolution of complex nervous systems.
source: Clustering of Nav channels at nodes of Ranvier is essential for efficient action potential propagation and has been proposed as a key event in the evolution of complex nervous systems (Hill et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: During development, two overlapping glia-dependent mechanisms rapidly cluster ankyrins and Nav channels.
source: During development, two overlapping glia-dependent mechanisms rapidly cluster ankyrins and Nav channels (Amor et al., 2017; Feinberg et al., 2010; Susuki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The nodal spectrin cytoskeleton normally consists of tetramers of two β4 and two α2 spectrin subunits.
source: The nodal spectrin cytoskeleton, normally consisting of tetramers of two β4 and two α2 spectrin subunits, has been proposed to perform this function.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of spectrin structure.

claim: Loss of both ankyrins completely blocked nodal Nav channel clustering during node assembly.
source: Loss of both ankyrins completely blocked nodal Nav channel clustering during node assembly.
evidence: This is stated as a result from previous experiments by the authors.

claim: In contrast to ankyrins, a nodal spectrin cytoskeleton is not required for the initial clustering of Nav channels.
source: Furthermore, removing both β1 and β4 spectrin from nodes simultaneously showed that in contrast to ankyrins, a nodal spectrin cytoskeleton is not required for the initial clustering of Nav channels (Figure 7)
evidence: This is supported by data showing Nav channels cluster at P8 in double knockout mice.

claim: β4 spectrin is recruited to nodes of Ranvier through binding to AnkG.
source: this observation is consistent with the fact that β4 spectrin is recruited to nodes of Ranvier through binding to AnkG (Jenkins et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Nodal β spectrins are necessary to maintain nodal Nav channel clusters.
source: Instead, we find that nodal β spectrins are necessary to maintain nodal Nav channel clusters (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by data showing progressive loss of Nav channels with age in double knockout mice.

claim: A β2 spectrin-dependent paranodal barrier can cluster nodal proteins during development.
source: Furthermore, although a β2 spectrin-dependent paranodal barrier can cluster nodal proteins during development (Amor et al., 2017), our results show that in the absence of nodal spectrins (α2/β1 and α2/β4), paranodal spectrins (α2/β2) are not sufficient to maintain Nav channel protein complexes
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: In the absence of nodal spectrins (α2/β1 and α2/β4), paranodal spectrins (α2/β2) are not sufficient to maintain Nav channel protein complexes.
source: Furthermore, although a β2 spectrin-dependent paranodal barrier can cluster nodal proteins during development (Amor et al., 2017), our results show that in the absence of nodal spectrins (α2/β1 and α2/β4), paranodal spectrins (α2/β2) are not sufficient to maintain Nav channel protein complexes
evidence: This is inferred from the progressive loss of Nav channels in double knockout mice despite intact paranodal domains.

claim: PNS nodal extracellular matrix molecules including gliomedin and NrCAM help to maintain proper nodal Nav channel densities.
source: Previous studies showed that PNS nodal extracellular matrix molecules including gliomedin and NrCAM help to maintain proper nodal Nav channel densities (Amor et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Both extracellular and intracellular interactions preserve nodal Nav channel clusters.
source: Our experiments extend these observations and show that both extracellular and intracellular interactions preserve nodal Nav channel clusters.
evidence: This is inferred from the current study showing intracellular spectrins are required for maintenance, combined with previous studies showing ECM molecules are also required.

claim: The normal function of β1 spectrin in axons remains unknown.
source: Thus, the normal function of β1 spectrin in axons remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the lack of phenotype in β1 spectrin knockout mice.

claim: β1 spectrin cannot compensate for β4 spectrin at AIS.
source: We speculate that β1 spectrin cannot compensate for β4 spectrin at AIS.
evidence: This is stated as speculation to explain the pathology in humans with β4 spectrin variants.

claim: Loss of AnkG disrupts neuronal polarity and causes axon degeneration.
source: Loss of AnkG disrupts neuronal polarity and causes axon degeneration (Hedstrom et al., 2008; Sobotzik et al., 2009; Zhou et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The periodic spectrin-actin cytoskeleton has been proposed to resist mechanical stresses and help to maintain the structural integrity of axons.
source: The periodic spectrin-actin cytoskeleton has been proposed to resist these stresses and help to maintain the structural integrity of axons (Krieg et al., 2017; Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Specifically and simultaneously ablating nodal β1 and β4 spectrin is sufficient to induce an axon injury response even though the remaining internodal and paranodal spectrin cytoskeletons remain intact.
source: We found that specifically and simultaneously ablating nodal β1 and β4 spectrin is sufficient to induce an axon injury response even though the remaining internodal and paranodal spectrin cytoskeletons remain intact.
evidence: This is supported by ATF3 expression data in double knockout mice.

claim: Mice lacking α2 spectrin in sensory neurons had a much stronger phenotype than mice lacking both β1 and β4 spectrin, with an axon injury response detectable in large diameter sensory neurons by two weeks of age and robust axon degeneration seen by electron microscopy as early as one week after birth.
source: On the other hand, mice lacking α2 spectrin in sensory neurons had a much stronger phenotype; an axon injury response was detectable in large diameter sensory neurons by two weeks of age and robust axon degeneration was seen by electron microscopy as early as one week after birth (Huang et al., 2017b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Mice lacking both β1 and β4 spectrin in sensory neurons showed a less severe axon injury response that was not detectable until the mice were 6 months old.
source: Mice lacking both β1 and β4 spectrin in sensory neurons showed a less severe axon injury response that was not detectable until the mice were 6 months old.
evidence: This is supported by ATF3 expression data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Loss of nodal spectrins creates intermittent 'breaks' in the spectrin cytoskeleton which gradually compromises the physical properties of the whole network.
source: We speculate that loss of nodal spectrins creates intermittent 'breaks' in the spectrin cytoskeleton which gradually compromises the physical properties of the whole network.
evidence: This is stated as speculation to explain the progressive axon injury phenotype.

claim: Axonal spectrins confer more stiffness to axons than the soma and dendrites.
source: Previous studies modeling the properties of a periodic arrangement of spectrins suggested they confer more stiffness to axons than the soma and dendrites, and that axonal spectrins are indeed under higher entropic tension due to its fully-stretched organization with 190 nm spacing (Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous modeling study.

claim: Axonal spectrins are under higher entropic tension due to their fully-stretched organization with 190 nm spacing.
source: Previous studies modeling the properties of a periodic arrangement of spectrins suggested they confer more stiffness to axons than the soma and dendrites, and that axonal spectrins are indeed under higher entropic tension due to its fully-stretched organization with 190 nm spacing (Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous modeling study.

claim: Scattered breaks in the spectrin network may not allow recovery to the initial 'under-tension' configuration.
source: Scattered breaks in the spectrin network may not allow recovery to the initial 'under-tension' configuration.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the mechanism of axon injury.

claim: Axons may progressively lose the ability to resist mechanical stresses and eventually degenerate due to breaks in the spectrin network.
source: Thus, axons may progressively lose the ability to resist mechanical stresses and eventually degenerate.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the consequence of spectrin network breaks.

claim: Nodes of Ranvier are a preferential site of Ca2+ entry in some diseases and injuries.
source: These observations on the role of nodal spectrins and axon integrity may have important implications for some diseases and injuries where nodes of Ranvier are a preferential site of Ca2+ entry.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge without specific citation.

claim: Elevated Ca2+ activates calpain proteases that efficiently degrade spectrin cytoskeletons.
source: Elevated Ca2+ activates calpain proteases that efficiently degrade spectrin cytoskeletons (Ma, 2013; Schafer et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Disruption of the nodal cytoskeleton may be one important component of peripheral nerve injury and a potential therapeutic point of intervention.
source: Thus, disruption of the nodal cytoskeleton may be one important component of peripheral nerve injury and a potential therapeutic point of intervention.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the implications of the findings.

claim: A hierarchy of β spectrins exists at nodes of Ranvier that are necessary to maintain nodal Nav channel clustering.
source: In conclusion, we provide evidence for a hierarchy of β spectrins at nodes of Ranvier that are necessary to maintain nodal Nav channel clustering.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing β4 is primary, β1 can substitute, and both are required for maintenance.

claim: Loss of nodal β spectrins is sufficient to induce an axon injury response.
source: Furthermore, we show that loss of nodal β spectrins is sufficient to induce an axon injury response.
evidence: This is supported by ATF3 expression and electron microscopy data in double knockout mice.

claim: Exons 29 and 30 of the mouse Sptbn4 gene are flanked by loxP sites in Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: To disrupt the function of β4 spectrin in axons we used a conditional null allele with exons 29 and 30 of the mouse Sptbn4 gene flanked by loxP sites (Sptbn4F/F mice; Unudurthi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the mouse model and supported by citation.

claim: In the presence of Cre recombinase, exons 29 and 30 of Sptbn4 are excised.
source: In the presence of Cre recombinase exons 29 and 30 are excised
evidence: This is stated as a description of how the conditional allele works.

claim: The excision of exons 29 and 30 of Sptbn4 is predicted to disrupt both β4Σ1 and β4Σ6 spectrin splice variants.
source: the excision of exons 29 and 30 is predicted to disrupt both β4Σ1 and β4Σ6 spectrin splice variants, the two major forms of β4 spectrin found at AIS and nodes of Ranvier (Komada and Soriano, 2002; Lacas-Gervais et al., 2004; Uemoto et al., 2007; Yoshimura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a prediction based on the gene structure and supported by citations about the splice variants.

claim: β4Σ1 and β4Σ6 spectrin splice variants are the two major forms of β4 spectrin found at AIS and nodes of Ranvier.
source: the excision of exons 29 and 30 is predicted to disrupt both β4Σ1 and β4Σ6 spectrin splice variants, the two major forms of β4 spectrin found at AIS and nodes of Ranvier (Komada and Soriano, 2002; Lacas-Gervais et al., 2004; Uemoto et al., 2007; Yoshimura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Both β4Σ1 and β4Σ6 spectrin splice variants are lost in Nes-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice.
source: Immunoblotting of brain homogenate with an antibody generated against the C-terminal SD domain found in β4Σ1 and β4Σ6 spectrin splice variants showed that both variants are lost in Nes-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: No AIS immunoreactivity for β4 spectrin was found in Nes-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice using both C- and N-terminal-directed β4 spectrin antibodies.
source: To further confirm the loss of AIS β4 spectrin and to verify that no truncated N-terminal fragments of β4Σ1 are at the AIS, we used both C- and N-terminal-directed β4 spectrin antibodies to immunolabel cortical neurons in Sptbn4F/F and Nes-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice; we found no AIS immunoreactivity in Nes-Cre;Sptbn4F/F mice (Figure 1B; note, the nuclear signal detected with the N-terminal-directed antibody is not specific to β4 spectrin).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The nuclear signal detected with the N-terminal-directed β4 spectrin antibody is not specific to β4 spectrin.
source: note, the nuclear signal detected with the N-terminal-directed antibody is not specific to β4 spectrin
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the immunostaining experiment.

claim: Avil-Cre mice were used to specifically eliminate β4 spectrin from peripheral sensory neurons.
source: To determine the function of β4 spectrin at nodes of Ranvier, and to circumvent the confound of loss of β4 spectrin from AIS, we crossed Sptbn4F/F mice to Advillin-Cre (Avil-Cre) mice to specifically eliminate β4 spectrin from peripheral sensory neurons.
evidence: This is stated as the experimental strategy.

claim: Using Avil-Cre mice enables a direct comparison between sensory dorsal roots (no β4 spectrin) and motor ventral roots (control) in the same mouse.
source: This strategy also enables a direct comparison between sensory dorsal roots (no β4 spectrin) and motor ventral roots (control) in the same mouse.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of the experimental design.

source: we generated a conditional null allele of β1 spectrin by flanking exon 2 of the mouse Sptb gene with loxP sites (SptbF/F mice); in the presence of Cre recombinase exon two is excised.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the mouse model generated.

claim: In the presence of Cre recombinase, exon 2 of Sptb is excised in SptbF/F mice.
source: we generated a conditional null allele of β1 spectrin by flanking exon 2 of the mouse Sptb gene with loxP sites (SptbF/F mice); in the presence of Cre recombinase exon two is excised.
evidence: This is stated as a description of how the conditional allele works.

source: Immunoblotting of brain homogenate and immunostaining of brain sections showed complete removal of neuronal β1 spectrin in Nes-Cre;SptbF/F mice (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Nes-Cre;SptbF/F mice show complete removal of neuronal β1 spectrin as confirmed by immunostaining of brain sections.
source: Immunoblotting of brain homogenate and immunostaining of brain sections showed complete removal of neuronal β1 spectrin in Nes-Cre;SptbF/F mice (Figure 3A,B).

source: To selectively and simultaneously eliminate β4 and β1 spectrins from nodes without affecting AIS spectrins, we generated Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice.
evidence: This is stated as the experimental strategy.

source: We found that Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice had severe defects in proprioception as indicated by hindlimb clasping (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is supported by observation shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice are ataxic.
source: We found that Avil-Cre;SptbF/F;Sptbn4F/F mice had severe defects in proprioception as indicated by hindlimb clasping (Figure 4A) and gait analysis (Figure 4B and Video 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the hindlimb clasping, gait abnormalities, and rotarod impairment.

claim: Mice lacking both β4 and β1 spectrins have a specific impairment at nodes of Ranvier.
source: However, consistent with a specific impairment at nodes of Ranvier, nociception as assayed by the tail immersion test, showed no significant difference in the latency to tail flick (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is inferred from the preserved nociception (unmyelinated axons) but impaired proprioception (myelinated axons with nodes).
